topic: How does the polarization diversity restriction in PR-based TAs influence network topology planning for global coverage satellites?
consensus_response: The polarization diversity restriction in Phased-Array Transceivers (TAS) affects network topology planning by limiting cell size and increasing inter-cell interference due to reduced capacity and increased side lobes. This necessitates a reevaluation of network topology planning for global coverage satellites, focusing on optimizing satellite orbits, altitudes, and constellation geometries to minimize interference between adjacent cells. Optimizing frequency reuse can mitigate this limitation, but may lead to higher costs associated with system design and implementation.
reference_context: The polarization diversity restriction affects the array factor of PR-based TAs, increasing side lobes and reducing gain due to the filtering effect. This makes PR TAS unsuitable for applications requiring polarization switching between adjacent cells, impacting network resource allocation and capacity planning.
